This code I want to try to do loops, where it just takes a dynamic name and changes it. 
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Load necessary library
library(imager)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
# All animals to process
IDs <- c("ID1", "ID3", "ID6", "ID7", "IDWT")

# Make sure output folder exists
if (!dir.exists(here("data"))) {
  dir.create(here("data"))
}

for (ID in IDs) {
  
  message("Processing ", ID, "...")
  
  # ============================================================
  # GFP / AF488
  # ============================================================
  
  image_dir <- here(
    "retinorecipient_images",
    ID,
    "AF488"
  )
  
  jpg_files <- list.files(
    image_dir,
    pattern = "\\.jpg$",
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )
  
  results_df <- data.frame(
    File = character(),
    GFP_Presence = character()
  )
  
  # Analyze each AF488 image
  for (file in jpg_files) {
    
    full_path <- file.path(image_dir, file)
    
    img <- load.image(full_path)
    
    thresh_val <- 0.5
    img_thresh <- img > thresh_val
    
    num_pixels_above_thresh <- sum(img_thresh)
    
    gfp_presence <- ifelse(
      num_pixels_above_thresh > 100,
      "Yes",
      "No"
    )
    
    results_df <- rbind(
      results_df,
      data.frame(
        File = file,
        GFP_Presence = gfp_presence
      )
    )
    
    rm(img, img_thresh)
    gc()
  }
  
  # Save GFP results
  file_name_gfp <- here(
    "data",
    paste0(
      "GFP_Presence_Results_",
      ID,
      ".csv"
    )
  )
  
  write.csv(
    results_df,
    file_name_gfp,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  
  # ============================================================
  # CTB / AF647
  # ============================================================
  
  ctb_image_dir <- here(
    "retinorecipient_images",
    ID,
    "AF647"
  )
  
  ctb_jpg_files <- list.files(
    ctb_image_dir,
    pattern = "\\.jpg$",
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )
  
  ctb_results_df <- data.frame(
    File = character(),
    CTB_Presence = character()
  )
  
  # Analyze each AF647 image
  for (file in ctb_jpg_files) {
    
    full_path <- file.path(
      ctb_image_dir,
      file
    )
    
    img <- load.image(full_path)
    
    thresh_val <- 0.5
    img_thresh <- img > thresh_val
    
    num_pixels_above_thresh <- sum(img_thresh)
    
    ctb_presence <- ifelse(
      num_pixels_above_thresh > 100,
      "Yes",
      "No"
    )
    
    ctb_results_df <- rbind(
      ctb_results_df,
      data.frame(
        File = file,
        CTB_Presence = ctb_presence
      )
    )
    
    rm(img, img_thresh)
    gc()
  }
  
  # Save CTB results
  file_name_ctb <- here(
    "data",
    paste0(
      "CTB_Presence_Results_",
      ID,
      ".csv"
    )
  )
  
  write.csv(
    ctb_results_df,
    file_name_ctb,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  
  # ============================================================
  # MERGE GFP + CTB
  # ============================================================
  
  gfp_df <- read_csv(
    file_name_gfp,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )
  
  ctb_df <- read_csv(
    file_name_ctb,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )
  
  # Remove channel identifier so corresponding sections match
  gfp_df <- gfp_df %>%
    mutate(
      merge_key = gsub(
        "_AF488",
        "",
        File
      )
    )
  
  ctb_df <- ctb_df %>%
    mutate(
      merge_key = gsub(
        "_AF647",
        "",
        File
      )
    )
  
  # Match AF488 and AF647 images
  merged_df <- inner_join(
    gfp_df,
    ctb_df,
    by = "merge_key"
  )
  
  # Determine sections containing both signals
  merged_df <- merged_df %>%
    mutate(
      Overlap = ifelse(
        GFP_Presence == "Yes" &
          CTB_Presence == "Yes",
        "Yes",
        "No"
      )
    )
  
  
  # ============================================================
  # SAVE MERGED RESULTS
  # ============================================================
  
  file_name_merge_all <- here(
    "data",
    paste0(
      "GFP_and_CTB_Overlap_Results_",
      ID,
      ".csv"
    )
  )
  
  write.csv(
    merged_df,
    file_name_merge_all,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  
  # Keep only overlapping sections
  overlap_df <- merged_df %>%
    filter(Overlap == "Yes")
  
  file_name_merge_yes <- here(
    "data",
    paste0(
      "GFP_and_CTB_Overlap_Only_",
      ID,
      ".csv"
    )
  )
  
  write.csv(
    overlap_df,
    file_name_merge_yes,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  message(
    ID,
    " complete: ",
    nrow(overlap_df),
    " overlapping sections found."
  )
}
```
